title: Does Deterministic Generate–Validate–Repair Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Changes? A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory study (n = 200 intent→configuration tasks) to test whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline that consults a deterministic NetOps validator reduces validator‑detected unsafe or semantically incorrect network changes relative to an LLM‑only generation pipeline. The run used a single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) under adapter‑enforced shared‑initial generation semantics and a primary deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed all planned pairs (complete_pair_count = 200) consuming 200 model calls (one shared initial generation per task); no repair calls were issued because every initial candidate passed the validator (baseline_success_count = 200/200; guarded_success_count = 200/200). Paired contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because baseline validator‑detected failures were 0% for this task bank under the chosen generation policy, the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis could not be meaningfully evaluated. We report the sealed design, deterministic enforcement evidence (adapter accounting and provider audit showing hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}), the Mininet 10% holdout that produced zero validator–emulator disagreements, and an artifact‑grounded discussion of interpretation, threats to validity, and recommendations for future studies (preregistration id: cnsms2026‑gvr‑effectiveness‑02).

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation with generative language models can materially accelerate NetOps work but exposes operations to incorrect or unsafe changes. Prior work therefore proposes grounding, deterministic validation, and repair loops (generate–validate–repair, GVR) to detect and correct unsafe candidates before application. The operational benefit of automated repair depends on (i) baseline prevalence of validator‑detectable failures under the chosen generation policy, (ii) validator coverage and fidelity, and (iii) the repair budget and repair‑prompt effectiveness. We preregistered a focused confirmatory question: Does an automated deterministic GVR pipeline that consults a deterministic NetOps validator materially reduce validator‑detected unsafe or semantically incorrect network changes relative to an LLM‑only generation pipeline on a curated 200‑task intent→configuration bank? The study used a paired shared‑initial design that fixes the generator output per task to isolate the marginal effect of invoking a validator and, if needed, a single automated repair on the identical candidate.
sections.related_work: Surveys and empirical studies document persistent LLM factual errors, prompt sensitivity, and non‑determinism, and they evaluate mitigations including retrieval grounding, verifier‑assisted repair, and guarded agent architectures. NetOps prototypes demonstrate intent→configuration feasibility but often lack instrumented, preregistered, or externally auditable failure‑rate studies. Architectural proposals recommend integrating deterministic validators (Batfish‑style or policy‑driven checkers) with LLM generation; independent red‑team audits emphasize configuration‑level brittleness and tool‑description injection vectors that can alter safety outcomes. Our work contributes an externally auditable, preregistered measurement isolating the incremental effect of a deterministic validator+single‑repair step on identical LLM outputs, thereby clarifying when GVR can or cannot reduce validator‑detectable errors for a fixed generator policy.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (id cnsms2026‑gvr‑effectiveness‑02) fixed a paired binary design with n = 200 tasks, one shared deterministic initial generation per task, and a repair budget of at most one automated repair call per task. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the primary test was an exact two‑sided McNemar test (α = 0.05). Confidence intervals were computed by the bootstrap percentile method (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Power planning assumed baseline unsafe incidence ≈30% and targeted a 50% relative reduction; those assumptions justified sample size but do not affect the recorded outcomes.

Task bank and validators. The confirmatory sample used a curated machine‑checkable intent→configuration bank (200 tasks, four topology clusters: enterprise, campus, datacenter, edge; 50 tasks each). Each task encoded initial/final states and workflow constraints (make‑before‑break, must_be_down_for_fields, group‑active minima). The primary deterministic checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforces syntax and intent/constraint checks and emits structured diagnostics including valid flag, violation_count, parsed_command_count, and required_command_count. A Mininet‑based data‑plane emulator was preregistered as an independent secondary disagreement detector applied to a randomized 10% holdout (20 tasks) to reveal validator blind spots.

Adapter semantics and determinism reconciliation. The confirmatory contrast required removing sampling variance across conditions; we therefore used a hosted adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) that enforced shared_initial generation semantics: for each task the system produced a single initial candidate that was reused in both the baseline (LLM‑only) and guarded (GVR) conditions. The archived model configuration declares requested_model = "gpt‑5‑mini" and lists "temperature": null; determinism in this run was achieved by adapter enforcement of shared‑initial generation rather than by relying on an explicit temperature numeric setting in the provider configuration. The execution accounting artifacts record hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, which demonstrate that exactly one shared model invocation occurred per task and that sampling variance across conditions was removed. Stating these concrete values (hosted_model_call_event_count = 200; stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200) reconciles the apparent ambiguity between a null temperature field and the observed deterministic shared‑initial behavior.

Repair policy, budgeting, and analysis. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one automated repair prompt to the same LLM when the primary validator reported violations; repaired candidates would be re‑validated by the primary validator. The execution contract enforced a maximum model‑call cap of 400 (200 initial + up to 200 repairs). The primary analysis used an exact McNemar test on the 2×2 paired table (n11, n10, n01, n00) and reported absolute and relative reductions with a bootstrap percentile CI. Secondary exploratory analyses (planned) included logistic regressions and descriptive summaries of repair iteration counts and model‑call costs; these remained conditional and were executed only if repair events occurred.

Reproducibility artifacts and conservative contamination rule. Core archived artifacts sufficient for independent audit are provided in the execution bundle (examples: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/contamination_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Per the preregistered contamination plan, any task in which primary validator verdict != Mininet emulator verdict would have been flagged and excluded from the primary analysis; the Mininet holdout summary reports zero disagreement flags. We note a documented reproducibility gap: the labeled artifact set does not include an explicit selection seed for the randomized Mininet 10% holdout draw, which prevents exact deterministic reconstruction of the exact holdout set even though the contamination summary records zero disagreements.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and basic outcomes. The run executed all planned episodes under the frozen preregistration (start and completion timestamps are recorded in the archived manifest). Model calls used = 200 (one shared initial generation per task); maximum_model_calls = 400; repair_calls_used = 0. Provider/adaptor audit fields record hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200}, confirming single shared initial invocations per task.

Validator results and paired contingency. Every initial candidate passed the primary deterministic validator: baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The paired contingency table is n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The observed paired difference estimate = 0.0. The prespecified exact McNemar two‑sided test yields p = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) produce a 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Because baseline validator failures were absent, the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not evaluable on this sample.

Repair and secondary outcomes. No validator failures were observed; consequently the preregistered automated repair branch was never invoked and the planned secondary estimands (average repair iterations per repaired task, GVR‑introduced failure rate, model‑call cost per successful repair) have no empirical data for this run and are recorded as empty in the analysis artifacts. The Mininet 10% holdout (20 tasks) produced zero disagreements between the primary validator and the emulator per the contamination summary.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per‑task validator traces show that shared initial outputs matched task required_sequence constraints and that validation_after.valid = true with violation_count = 0. Difficulty annotations across tasks include labels such as "medium", "hard", and "very_hard" with dependency patterns (make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change, rolling_access_vlan_migration), demonstrating that the task bank exercised nontrivial constraints even though the generator outputs satisfied them under the frozen generation policy.
sections.discussion:
Conditional interpretation. The degenerate paired outcome (no discordant pairs) is an artifact‑grounded observation: under the chosen generator/prompting policy and the enforced single shared draw per task, validator‑detectable failures did not occur in this curated sample. Statistically, when n10 and n01 are zero the exact McNemar test is uninformative about treatment superiority; the observed p = 1.0 and bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0] accurately reflect that no paired difference was observed. This should not be overinterpreted as a universal statement about GVR effectiveness: rather, it is a conditional statement about the marginal value of automated repair given (A) the specific model (gpt‑5‑mini), (B) the shared deterministic single‑draw generation policy (adapter enforced), and (C) the particular 200‑task bank.

Why initial candidates passed. Several concrete archived indicators explain the null result. First, required_command_count values recorded in validator traces matched parsed_command_count for representative tasks, indicating the generator produced sequences that fulfilled encoded workflow constraints. Second, difficulty labels in validator traces show the task bank included complex dependency patterns; correctness under those labels implies the generator/prompting policy produced constraint‑satisfying sequences rather than trivial or incomplete outputs. Third, adapter and provider accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 200; stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200) confirm that sampling variance was intentionally removed by the shared_initial design.

Methodological tradeoffs and recommendations. The shared_initial paired contrast isolates the incremental effect of validation+repair on a fixed generator output but does not measure unconditional operational failure risk (the probability the generator will produce a failing candidate on an independent application). For estimating unconditional failure prevalence and unconditional repair benefit, designs with independent per‑condition multi‑sample draws and nonzero sampling temperature or multiple draws per task are preferable. Practically, before deploying GVR practitioners should (1) measure baseline validator failure prevalence on representative operational workloads under the intended generation policy, (2) expand validator fidelity (richer device/vendor models and larger emulation/testbed checks) to detect oracle blind spots, and (3) consider multi‑sample generation and larger repair budgets if baseline failures are nontrivial. The archived artifacts here document the accounting and the conservative contamination detection procedure that supported these recommendations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is strengthened by preregistration, deterministic adapter enforcement, and deterministic reconciliation artifacts that confirm episode accounting. Construct validity depends on validator expressiveness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a defined set of syntactic and intent constraints but does not capture all real device idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by the single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini), the shared_initial deterministic sampling policy, and the curated task bank. Conclusion validity is constrained because zero discordant observations render the preregistered relative‑reduction hypothesis unevaluable in this run.

Reproducibility note. The execution bundle provides the key artifacts necessary to audit the design and results (listed above). One documented reproducibility gap remains: the labeled artifact set does not include the explicit randomized selection seed used to draw the Mininet 10% holdout, which prevents exact deterministic reconstruction of the precise holdout selection even though the contamination summary reports zero disagreements for the holdout.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study (n = 200) comparing LLM‑only generation to a deterministic GVR pipeline using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, both pipelines produced validator‑passing configurations for every task (n11 = 200; no discordant pairs), yielding an observed paired difference of 0.0, exact McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Because baseline validator failures were absent under the chosen generation policy and task bank, the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis could not be evaluated. The artifact‑grounded result emphasizes that GVR’s marginal value is workload dependent: when validator‑detectable failures are rare under a production generator/prompt policy, a single‑pass automated repair budget yields no measured benefit for validator‑detected errors. Future confirmatory studies should (i) target workloads with nontrivial baseline failure rates, (ii) increase repair budgets and allow multi‑step or human‑in‑the‑loop repairs, (iii) evaluate independent multi‑sample generation policies to estimate unconditional failure rates, and (iv) expand validator fidelity with larger emulation or device checks. All core execution and analysis artifacts are archived under the preregistration id referenced below for independent inspection.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (mandatory). This study executed under the autonomous post‑lock preregistration cnsms2026‑gvr‑effectiveness‑02. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider label: openai_responses) invoked via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Topic constraints: the human Research Director limited the study to Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps focusing on safety/reliability of generated network changes. Frameworks and tools: orchestration used hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the deterministic task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Primary deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (intent/constraint checks). A Mininet‑based emulator was preregistered and executed as a secondary disagreement detector on a randomized 10% holdout (20 tasks); the archived contamination summary reports zero disagreements for that holdout. Preregistration and freeze: the experimental plan (estimand, sample size n = 200, paired shared‑initial design, stopping rules, max model calls = 400, repair budget = 1 per task) was frozen before any model calls. Autonomous execution and artifacts: the run executed autonomously under the frozen plan; model calls, prompts, seeds, validator traces, emulator traces, logs, and the artifact manifest are archived in the execution bundle. Model‑call budget and usage: 200 model calls were used (one shared initial generation per task); up to 200 repair calls were allowed but none were applied because initial candidates passed the validator. Human involvement: the human Research Director selected the topic family and pre‑lock constraints; no human manual editing or selective rewriting of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. Deviations and restarts: no post‑preregistration design changes or technical restarts occurred. Known reproducibility gap: the explicit randomized selection seed used to draw the Mininet 10% holdout is not present as a labeled artifact in the archive; this absence prevents exact deterministic reconstruction of the drawn holdout despite the contamination summary reporting no disagreements.
limitations: Task‑bank scope: the confirmatory sample used a curated synthetic/public intent→configuration bank (n = 200); results therefore reflect this bank and may not generalize to broader production workloads or adversarial distributions.

Single‑model and shared‑initial setting: only gpt‑5‑mini (hosted) with adapter‑enforced shared‑initial generation was tested (hosted_model_call_event_count = 200; stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200). Outcomes may differ across model families, independent per‑condition sampling, nonzero temperature sampling, or larger repair budgets.

Validator coverage and oracle limitations: the primary deterministic validator enforces a defined set of syntax/intent constraints; validators can fail to capture real device idiosyncrasies, vendor‑specific behaviors, or emergent failure modes detectable only by end‑to‑end deployment.

Adversarial robustness untested: this confirmatory run did not include active adversarial injection or red‑team tool‑description attacks; prior audits indicate such vectors can bypass naive defenses and remain a separate concern.

Reproducibility gap for contamination check: the randomized holdout selection seed for the Mininet contamination check is absent from the labeled artifacts, preventing exact reconstruction of the holdout selection.

Single repair budget: the GVR pipeline allowed at most one automated repair prompt per task; multi‑step repair strategies, different repair budgets, or human‑in‑the‑loop approvals were not exercised here.
